issues.t: Timing belt overdue
issues.sym: Usually no warning before it fails. When the belt breaks, the engine stops at once and won't restart.
issues.why: The 3.0L V6 uses a rubber timing belt that wears out with age. This is an interference engine, so a broken belt can let the valves hit the pistons and ruin the engine.
issues.next: Look for proof of a recent timing belt change. If there is none, have the belt (and usually the water pump) replaced before relying on the car.

issues.t: Cracked exhaust manifolds
issues.sym: A ticking or puffing noise from the engine that is loudest on a cold start, an exhaust smell, or a check engine light.
issues.why: The cast exhaust manifolds crack from years of heating and cooling. An owner reported to NHTSA that hot exhaust escaping near other parts could start an engine fire.
issues.next: Don't ignore exhaust smells in the cabin. Have the manifolds inspected and replaced if cracked.

issues.t: Hesitation or bucking from a bad knock sensor
issues.sym: Hesitation or bucking when you accelerate and weak power. The check engine light usually stays off.
issues.why: The knock sensor and its wiring sit under the intake manifold and become brittle. When the sensor fails, the computer retards timing and the engine feels flat.
issues.next: Have the codes read (knock sensor code 34). The intake has to come off, so replace the sensor's wiring harness at the same time. Use 91 octane fuel.

issues.t: Harsh shifts or slipping automatic transmission
issues.sym: A hard or slipping shift from first to second, especially when cold, or erratic shifting.
issues.why: Some harsh shifting is normal until the transmission warms up, but these heavy cars also wear out transmissions faster in hot climates, especially with old fluid.
issues.next: Let the car warm up before driving hard. If shifts stay harsh when warm or it slips, have the fluid and codes checked soon. An extra transmission cooler helps in hot areas.

issues.t: Hard to start when hot or won't start at times
issues.sym: The engine cranks but won't start, often after it has been driven and parked for a short time.
issues.why: Owners of this generation report hot-start problems and intermittent no-starts at high mileage, often traced to ignition or fuel delivery parts.
issues.next: Note when it happens. Have a shop check for spark and fuel pressure while the car is in the no-start condition.

issues.t: Low or unstable idle from a dirty throttle body
issues.sym: The idle is low, rough or hunts up and down, and the engine may stall when you come to a stop.
issues.why: Varnish builds up in the throttle body and blocks the small air passage the engine needs at idle.
issues.next: A throttle body cleaning usually fixes it. If not, have the idle air control parts checked.

issues.t: Check engine light from EVAP purge valve
issues.sym: Check engine light on, with no change in how the car drives.
issues.why: The canister purge valve in the evaporative emissions system fails.
issues.next: Make sure the fuel cap is tight, then have the codes read.

issues.t: Headlights go out (relay)
issues.sym: Both headlights suddenly stop working, or they work only some of the time.
issues.why: The headlight relay fails, often after higher-wattage bulbs are fitted, which overload the relay and wiring.
issues.next: Don't drive at night without headlights. Have the relay replaced and use bulbs that match the original wattage.

issues.t: Clogged sunroof drains leak water inside
issues.sym: Water on the headliner, floor or seats after rain or a car wash, or electrical faults after it rains.
issues.why: The sunroof drain tubes clog, so water overflows into the cabin. Owners warn that water can reach and damage the engine computer.
issues.next: Clear the drains. If the car has electrical faults after rain, have the engine computer area checked for water.

issues.t: Sunroof motor stops working
issues.sym: The sunroof won't open or close.
issues.why: The sunroof motor or mechanism wears out with age. Owners describe the repair as expensive and time-consuming.
issues.next: Close the roof by hand if possible to keep water out, then get a repair quote.

issues.t: Power windows fail or move by themselves
issues.sym: A window stops moving, moves slowly, or a window goes down on its own in the rain.
issues.why: Window regulators and motors wear out; water can also get into the window switches.
issues.next: Have the switch, motor and regulator tested before replacing parts.

issues.t: Alternator failure
issues.sym: The battery light comes on, the lights dim, or the battery keeps going dead.
issues.why: The alternator wears out with age. Long-time owners say rebuilt aftermarket units often fail early.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested. Owners recommend a genuine or high-quality replacement.

issues.t: Thermostat housing coolant leak
issues.sym: Coolant drips at the front of the engine, a sweet smell, or the coolant level dropping.
issues.why: The thermostat housing or its gasket starts to leak with age.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge and stop if it climbs. Have the housing and gasket replaced.

issues.t: Rust at the bottom of doors and rear panels
issues.sym: Bubbling paint or rust at the bottom of the doors or on the panels below the rear doors.
issues.why: Water collects at the door seams and lower panels, and road salt speeds up rust.
issues.next: Catch rust early; small spots are much cheaper to repair than holes.

issues.t: Bose radio stops working
issues.sym: The factory Bose radio goes silent, cuts out or won't turn on.
issues.why: The factory radio and amplifier fail with age; owners call this a common issue.
issues.next: Check fuses first, then consider a rebuilt factory unit or an aftermarket radio.

issues.t: Worn control arm bushings and struts
issues.sym: Clunks over bumps, a loose feel in the steering, uneven tire wear, or a bouncy ride.
issues.why: Rubber bushings and struts wear out with age. Some suspension parts are only available from Infiniti.
issues.next: Have the front end inspected and the alignment checked after repairs.

issues.t: Power door locks act up
issues.sym: One or more doors won't lock or unlock with the switch or remote, or work only some of the time.
issues.why: Door lock actuators wear out. Owners report this on the driver's door and on several doors one after another.
issues.next: Have the actuator in the affected door replaced.

issues.t: A/C stops cooling on long trips
issues.sym: The A/C blows cold at first, then warm air during long drives.
issues.why: Owners of this generation report the A/C cutting out after long trips. Low refrigerant or a freezing evaporator are common reasons.
issues.next: Have the A/C pressures checked and look for leaks before simply recharging.

issues.t: Dash lights stay on or won't dim
issues.sym: The dashboard lights stay at one brightness or flicker.
issues.why: The dashboard dimmer switch wears out.
issues.next: Have the dimmer switch replaced.

issues.t: Parking brake won't fully release
issues.sym: The parking brake pedal doesn't fully release, the brake light stays on, or the rear brakes drag and smell hot.
issues.why: The parking brake release or cables stick with age.
issues.next: Don't drive with the parking brake dragging; it can overheat the rear brakes. Have the cables and release checked.
